Definition: from a compound of G5495 and τείνω (to stretch); to be a hand-reacher or voter (by raising the hand), i.e. (generally) to select or appoint:--choose, ordain.
BiblicalUsage: To appoint by stretching out the hand is the word for choosing elders and messengers. Paul and Barnabas ordain elders in every church with prayer and fasting, and the churches choose a brother to travel with Paul in the grace.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the stretched-out hand is the church's way of choosing: elders are appointed by the people and commended to the Lord, and the choice is made in prayer.
RelatedEvents: The Return Journey and the Appointment of Elders
